import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LaurentNilpotentCoeff

/-!
# EVERY UNIT CONGRUENT TO `1` MODULO NILPOTENTS IS A ℙ¹ COBOUNDARY

`Algebra/LaurentNilpotentCoboundary.lean` proves that `1 + C e · f` is a two-chart coboundary when
`e` is nilpotent — the **single-generator** case, where the whole nilpotent deformation is a
multiple of one element `e`.  The arbitrary-ring ℙ¹ Picard computation needs the **multi-generator**
statement: a Laurent unit `1 + z` with `z` an *arbitrary* nilpotent Laurent polynomial (whose
coefficients generate an arbitrary nilpotent ideal, not a principal one) is a coboundary.

This file proves that.  It is the keystone that `Algebra/LaurentReducedReduction.lean` needs but
does not contain: with the reduced-ring characterisation (`Algebra/LaurentCoboundaryReduced.lean`)
it upgrades the ℙ¹ coboundary computation from reduced rings to **arbitrary** commutative rings —
`Pic(ℙ¹_A)` is computed with no domain, reducedness, or field hypothesis.

## The mechanism: halving on ideal powers

The single-generator proof halves the nilpotency *index* by squaring the deforming element.  Here
the deformation is along a whole ideal `I` (generated by `z`'s coefficients), so we halve on the
*ideal power*: the induction is over `n` with `I ^ (2 ^ n) = ⊥`.

Given `z` with all coefficients in `I`, split `z = P + Q` into its non-negative-degree part
`P = toLaurent (posPoly z)` (a unit of the left chart `A[t]`, since `posPoly z` is nilpotent) and
its negative-degree part `Q = rightChart (negPoly z)` (a unit of the right chart `A[t⁻¹]`).  Their
product is a coboundary `c` with

`c = (1 + P)(1 + Q) = 1 + z + P·Q`,

and the **cross term `P·Q` has coefficients in `I²`** (`coeff_mul_mem_mul`).  So the residual
`c⁻¹ · (1 + z) = 1 - c⁻¹ · P·Q` is `1 + w` with `w`'s coefficients in `I²`, and `(I²) ^ (2 ^ (n-1))
= I ^ (2 ^ n) = ⊥`: the induction hypothesis applies to `w`, and coboundaries are a subgroup, so
`1 + z = c · (c⁻¹ (1 + z))` is a coboundary.  The cross term is fed back at twice the ideal power,
exactly as the single-generator proof feeds it back at twice the element's nilpotency order.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.laurentCoboundary_one_add_of_coeffs_mem` — the ideal-power halving: if
  `I ^ (2 ^ n) = ⊥` and every coefficient of `z` is in `I`, then `1 + z` is a coboundary.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.nilpotent_one_add_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — **the headline**: a unit
  congruent to `1` modulo an arbitrary nilpotent Laurent polynomial is a coboundary.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory LaurentPolynomial

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]

/-! ## The two chart truncations of a Laurent polynomial -/

/-- The non-negative-degree part of `z`, as a genuine polynomial (left chart `A[t]`). -/
noncomputable def posPoly (z : LaurentPolynomial A) : Polynomial A :=
  ∑ i ∈ z.support.filter (0 ≤ ·), Polynomial.monomial i.toNat (z i)

/-- The negative-degree part of `z`, as a polynomial in the right chart coordinate `t⁻¹`. -/
noncomputable def negPoly (z : LaurentPolynomial A) : Polynomial A :=
  ∑ i ∈ z.support.filter (¬ 0 ≤ ·), Polynomial.monomial (-i).toNat (z i)

/-- `rightChart` on a monomial: `X ↦ T (-1)`, so `monomial n c ↦ C c · T (-n)`. -/
theorem rightChart_monomial (c : A) (n : ℕ) :
    rightChart A (Polynomial.monomial n c)
      = LaurentPolynomial.C c * LaurentPolynomial.T (-(n : ℤ)) := by
  rw [← Polynomial.C_mul_X_pow_eq_monomial, map_mul, rightChart_C, map_pow, rightChart_X,
    LaurentPolynomial.T_pow]
  congr 2
  ring

/-- Coefficients of the left-chart truncation lie in any ideal containing `z`'s coefficients. -/
theorem posPoly_coeff_mem {I : Ideal A} {z : LaurentPolynomial A} (hz : ∀ i, z i ∈ I) (m : ℕ) :
    (posPoly z).coeff m ∈ I := by
  classical
  unfold posPoly
  rw [Polynomial.finsetSum_coeff]
  refine Ideal.sum_mem _ (fun i _ => ?_)
  rw [Polynomial.coeff_monomial]
  split
  · exact hz i
  · exact Ideal.zero_mem _

/-- Coefficients of the right-chart truncation lie in any ideal containing `z`'s coefficients. -/
theorem negPoly_coeff_mem {I : Ideal A} {z : LaurentPolynomial A} (hz : ∀ i, z i ∈ I) (m : ℕ) :
    (negPoly z).coeff m ∈ I := by
  classical
  unfold negPoly
  rw [Polynomial.finsetSum_coeff]
  refine Ideal.sum_mem _ (fun i _ => ?_)
  rw [Polynomial.coeff_monomial]
  split
  · exact hz i
  · exact Ideal.zero_mem _

/-- The left-chart truncation, evaluated coefficientwise. -/
theorem toLaurent_posPoly_apply (z : LaurentPolynomial A) (j : ℤ) :
    (Polynomial.toLaurent (posPoly z)) j = if 0 ≤ j then z j else 0 := by
  classical
  unfold posPoly
  rw [map_sum]
  have hterm : ∀ i ∈ z.support.filter (0 ≤ ·),
      Polynomial.toLaurent (Polynomial.monomial i.toNat (z i))
        = (Finsupp.single i (z i) : LaurentPolynomial A) := by
    intro i hi
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hi
    rw [Polynomial.toLaurent_C_mul_T, ← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T,
      Int.toNat_of_nonneg hi.2]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm]
  change (Finset.sum (z.support.filter (0 ≤ ·))
    (fun i => (Finsupp.single i (z i) : ℤ →₀ A)) : ℤ →₀ A) j = _
  rw [Finset.sum_apply']
  simp only [Finsupp.single_apply]
  by_cases hj : 0 ≤ j
  · rw [if_pos hj]
    by_cases hmem : j ∈ z.support.filter (0 ≤ ·)
    · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single j]
      · rw [if_pos rfl]
      · intro b _ hbj; rw [if_neg hbj]
      · intro h; exact absurd hmem h
    · rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero]
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter, not_and] at hmem
        by_cases hjs : j ∈ z.support
        · exact absurd hj (hmem hjs)
        · rw [Finsupp.notMem_support_iff] at hjs; rw [hjs]
      · intro b hb; rw [if_neg]; rintro rfl; exact hmem hb
  · rw [if_neg hj, Finset.sum_eq_zero]
    intro b hb
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hb
    rw [if_neg]; rintro rfl; exact hj hb.2

/-- The right-chart truncation, evaluated coefficientwise. -/
theorem rightChart_negPoly_apply (z : LaurentPolynomial A) (j : ℤ) :
    (rightChart A (negPoly z)) j = if ¬ 0 ≤ j then z j else 0 := by
  classical
  unfold negPoly
  rw [map_sum]
  have hterm : ∀ i ∈ z.support.filter (¬ 0 ≤ ·),
      rightChart A (Polynomial.monomial (-i).toNat (z i))
        = (Finsupp.single i (z i) : LaurentPolynomial A) := by
    intro i hi
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hi
    rw [rightChart_monomial, ← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C_mul_T]
    congr 1
    have : (0 : ℤ) ≤ -i := by omega
    rw [Int.toNat_of_nonneg this]; ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm]
  change (Finset.sum (z.support.filter (¬ 0 ≤ ·))
    (fun i => (Finsupp.single i (z i) : ℤ →₀ A)) : ℤ →₀ A) j = _
  rw [Finset.sum_apply']
  simp only [Finsupp.single_apply]
  by_cases hj : ¬ 0 ≤ j
  · rw [if_pos hj]
    by_cases hmem : j ∈ z.support.filter (¬ 0 ≤ ·)
    · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single j]
      · rw [if_pos rfl]
      · intro b _ hbj; rw [if_neg hbj]
      · intro h; exact absurd hmem h
    · rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero]
      · rw [Finset.mem_filter, not_and] at hmem
        by_cases hjs : j ∈ z.support
        · exact absurd hj (hmem hjs)
        · rw [Finsupp.notMem_support_iff] at hjs; rw [hjs]
      · intro b hb; rw [if_neg]; rintro rfl; exact hmem hb
  · rw [if_neg hj, Finset.sum_eq_zero]
    intro b hb
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hb
    rw [if_neg]; rintro rfl; exact hj hb.2

/-- The two truncations reconstruct `z`. -/
theorem posPoly_add_negPoly (z : LaurentPolynomial A) :
    Polynomial.toLaurent (posPoly z) + rightChart A (negPoly z) = z := by
  apply Finsupp.ext
  intro j
  have hsum : (Polynomial.toLaurent (posPoly z) + rightChart A (negPoly z)) j
      = (Polynomial.toLaurent (posPoly z)) j + (rightChart A (negPoly z)) j := rfl
  rw [hsum, toLaurent_posPoly_apply, rightChart_negPoly_apply]
  by_cases hj : 0 ≤ j <;> simp [hj]

end AlgebraicGeometry
